about: WHAT WE KNOW ABOUT THE RADIOS PEOPLE ACTUALLY OWN.
MeshCore's companion protocol describes a radio's SETTINGS — frequency,
spreading factor, power — and says nothing about its HARDWARE. A board
with no GPS is not defective and does not report itself as lacking one:
it simply answers 0/0 forever, which is a real place in the Gulf of
Guinea and therefore refused as a position. Everything downstream of that
refusal (an empty ring, no bearings, 316 peers that cannot be drawn) is
correct behaviour that looks exactly like a broken app.
So the app carries its own knowledge. This file is that knowledge, and it
grows every time a new board is put on the bench.
OBSERVATION OUTRANKS THIS FILE. What a radio actually does is a fact;
what this catalogue says about its model is a guess about which model it
is. RadioFacts records the first, DeviceBook supplies the second, and
where they disagree the radio in the room wins.
confidence: 'tested' = connected to this board ourselves and watched it.
'reported' = public documentation, not yet on our bench.
null in caps means UNKNOWN — which is different from false, and the UI
must never turn an unknown into a claim.

devices.name: M5STACK C6L
devices.note: Bench radio B727FE05, 2026-08-16: reported 0.0/0.0 for a whole session while holding 350 contacts, 316 of them positioned. Operator confirmed the board carries no GPS. This is the device that taught us the empty ring needs an explanation.

devices.name: HELTEC LORA 32 V3
devices.note: 0.96 inch OLED, so it can display a pairing code. No GNSS.

devices.name: LILYGO T-BEAM
devices.note: GNSS on board — the radio can supply its own position, and then the headset fallback is never needed.

devices.name: LILYGO T-DECK
devices.note: Has a screen and a keyboard. The T-Deck PLUS is a different entry: it adds GNSS.

devices.name: RAK4631 WISBLOCK
devices.note: Modular: GNSS and display are separate WisBlock modules, so both are genuinely unknown until this radio is watched. Do not guess on this one.

devices.name: XIAO ESP32S3 + WIO SX1262
devices.note: No screen: a pairing code cannot be shown on the device, so pairing guidance that says 'read the code off the radio' is wrong for this board.
